# abseil-cpp / string_escape_fuzzer

OSS-Fuzz's fuzz target `string_escape_fuzzer` ([source](source/string_escape_fuzzer.cc), unmodified) over abseil-cpp (abseil/abseil-cpp at 926f1d05).

Checks 4 properties (listed below); the first, a round trip: CUnescape(CHexEscape(s)) == s, CUnescape(CEscape(s)) == s, CUnescape(Utf8SafeCEscape(s)) == s and CUnescape(Utf8SafeCHexEscape(s)) == s for every input byte string (CUnescape return value ignored, but the full output is compared).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against abseil-cpp at commit 926f1d05.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- CUnescape(CHexEscape(s)) == s, CUnescape(CEscape(s)) == s, CUnescape(Utf8SafeCEscape(s)) == s and CUnescape(Utf8SafeCHexEscape(s)) == s for every input byte string (CUnescape return value ignored, but the full output is compared) ([lines 24-42](source/string_escape_fuzzer.cc#L24-L42)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Meant as Base64Escape/Base64Unescape round trip, but line 47 compares str against `unescaped`, which still holds CUnescape(Utf8SafeCHexEscape(str)) from lines 39-40 (not the CHexEscape result). Line 41 has already required that to equal str, so this check is always true and the Base64 round trip is never checked (a bug in the harness) ([lines 44-48](source/string_escape_fuzzer.cc#L44-L48)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- WebSafeBase64Unescape(WebSafeBase64Escape(s)) == s ([lines 50-53](source/string_escape_fuzzer.cc#L50-L53)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Meant as HexStringToBytes(BytesToHexString(s)) == s, but the check compares str against `decoded` (the WebSafeBase64 result) instead of `bytes_result`, so the hex round trip is never checked (a bug in the harness) ([lines 55-59](source/string_escape_fuzzer.cc#L55-L59)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
